text:
marta: Quick sync — I'd like to lock a small 'cascading quantization' contract before we ship more low-bit lanes. Problem: runtime keeps hopping lanes under load and we don't have a shared definition of 'acceptable quality' to gate fallbacks. Can we agree metrics + minimal runtime API?
chris: Are we talking the usual FP8 -> INT8 -> 4bit cascade? what's the intended fallback granularity (per-request vs per-layer)?
kai: Yes FP8->INT8->4bit for now. Prefer per-request lane switching only; per-layer dynamic is extra complexity for now (but we may allow experimental hooks).
marta: Agreed on fallback order. The tradeoffs we need to capture: customer-visible quality delta, cost savings, and latency change. Also need a simple aggregate so routing/rollouts can make decisions.
oliver: Proposal for telemetry set: `perplexity_delta`, `token_degen_rate`, `mean_embedding_shift`, `latency_p50`, `latency_p95`, `cost_per_token`, `fallback_count`. Short, actionable.
kai: +1 to telemetry. Add `sampled_reference_prompts` id so ops can tie to offline evals. Note: embedding_shift is prompt-set dependent.
oliver: I want a single heuristic called `degradation_score` that the runtime emits. Example:
```
# normalized values in [0,1] relative to endpoint baseline
degradation_score = 0.6 * perplexity_delta_norm + 0.3 * token_degen_rate_norm + 0.1 * embedding_shift_norm
```
chris: Slight pushback — perplexity is model/token-length sensitive. We should compute normalized deltas against an endpoint-specific baseline (per-customer when private). Also we need to expose individual components for debugging.
marta: Good point. My contract suggestion: a `QuantProfile` that shipping teams provide with fields: `allowed_lanes: ["fp8","int8","int4"]`, `baseline_metrics_id`, `degrade_threshold` (float), `quality_budget` (minutes/day or tokens), `fallback_priority` (ordered list), `telemetry_keys` (list), `escrow_prompts` (ids array). Something like: 
```
QuantProfile = {
  "allowed_lanes": ["fp8","int8","int4"],
  "degrade_threshold": 0.2,
  "quality_budget_tokens": 100000,
  "baseline_metrics_id": "baseline-2026-03-01",
  "telemetry_keys": ["degradation_score","perplexity_delta","token_degen_rate","mean_embedding_shift","latency_p95"]
}
```
chris: We should also have an opt-in `strict_mode` for endpoints that cannot tolerate any visible delta (enterprise customers). In strict_mode runtime must not drop below FP8 unless manually approved.
kai: For Private deployments, baseline storage and baseline prompts can be customer-owned; the runtime should accept a `baseline_hash` reference rather than copy the prompts. Privacy-friendly.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary job `quant-metrics-collector#523` started for eng-ml/cascading-quant (CI).
oliver: Runtime API changes: each inference response should include `active_lane` and `last_degradation_score` in headers (or a debug payload), plus a `/admin/quant/status?endpoint=...` admin endpoint that returns current lane, recent scores, and recent fallback_count. Also add a header `x-quality-override` (bool) that the caller can set (rate-limited) to prefer quality over cost.
marta: We must be careful with `x-quality-override` — only allow for higher-tier customers and guard it with token-level quotas. No per-token negotiation. Keep it per-request.
chris: Rollout/ops checklist I propose: 1) offline eval vs escrow prompts (5k) produce baseline metrics, 2) canary at 0.5% traffic with full telemetry retention, 3) 5% with automatic rollback if `degradation_score` > `degrade_threshold` for 10 continuous minutes, 4) gradual ramp with daily budget checks.
kai: Who owns `quality_budget` enforcement? Product sets policy, ops enforces runtime metering. Need a playbook for owners.
marta: I'll write an RFC follow-up that includes the QuantProfile JSON schema, the degradation_score formula (and configuration knobs), example telemetry events, and a canary playbook. Action items: @chris write the offline eval harness, @kai add telemetry fields to the collector, @oliver add runtime endpoints + header support. Can everyone ack or drop concerns? :thumbsup:
chris: ack :thumbsup:
kai: ack
oliver: ack
marta: Thanks — I'll draft the RFC today and ping for review.
